text:
Steven Stamkos is 36 and ranks 3rd of 506 skaters in our wins added, a measure of how much each goal swung a game. Ten goals in 17 games, 12 power-play points, and Nashville had won four straight through Nov. 7. Andrew Brunette called the Predators "his team," per The Tennessean's headline, and Yahoo Sports noted he has moved into the all-time top five for power-play goals.

The caution is easy to spot. He is shooting 23% on 6.9 expected goals, above his 20% from last season, and his team has scored 4.7 more goals than expected with him on the ice. At 5-on-5 the Predators get only 45% of expected goals when he plays, so the even-strength play hasn't matched the finishing.

The flip side: Evolving-Hockey had him producing well below his chances in 2025-26, so his finishing has swung from one side to the other. Expect fewer goals from here, still mostly on the power play. Our range has him at 31 to 47 goals.
headline: Stamkos at 36 is still winning games in Nashville
